annotation.summary_en: China's November 2022 position paper on AI ethical governance sets out recommendations for governments on regulation, R&D, utilization and international cooperation. It promotes people-centred, controllable, trustworthy AI, tiered risk management, ethics review, and inclusive international rule-making. It contains no robotics-specific provisions.
key_provisions_or_claims: Governments should build AI ethics rules, accountability mechanisms and ethics review, with agile, tiered and categorized risk management.
R&D entities should embed ethics, ensure AI stays under human control, and make AI verifiable, traceable and trustworthy.
Prohibit AI uses contrary to law and ethics; set up emergency and compensation mechanisms.
Safeguard privacy and data security; strengthen public AI ethics education.
Pursue inclusive international AI governance frameworks respecting national practices and opposing exclusive blocs.
